100% Weapon Damage added to primary Bolt (not secondary Bolts)

Lightning Fury releases one secondary Bolt upon impact with an enemy, and one additional Bolt targeting each other enemy within 10 Yards, up to (Maximum Number of Bolts).

Lightning Fury's primary projectile releases its Bolts upon every impact with an enemy (and has no Next Hit Delay), making Pierce Chance particularly valuable for this skill. Secondary Bolts always Pierce.

  • Power Strike: +3% Lightning Damage per Level
  • Lightning Bolt: +3% Lightning Damage per Level

This equipment improves Damage, Attack Speed, Defense, and other Attributes. Chance to Cast effects from the equipment are functional.

  • Decoy: +20 Strength per Level (results in 15% Enhanced Damage per Level from Spear Strength scaling)
  • Pierce: +2% Lightning Resistance Pierce per Level
  • Penetrate: +40 Attack Rating per Level
  • Power Strike: +20% Lightning Damage per Level (only affects Nova Damage)
  • Critical Strike
Note: Valkyries are given your Hard Level of Critical Strike and receive that Skill's full effect.

Season 3:

  • Tiger strike attack rating per level reduced from 20% to 10%
  • Tiger strike now attacks with both weapons (requires dual claws)

Season 2:

  • Charge-up skills reworked
    • Instead of charges being generated one-at-a-time per charge-up attack and the effects only applying when consumed by a finishing move or normal attack:
    • Charge-up attacks immediately apply the attacks' effect of the appropriate stage (1-3) and generate charges until the character has that many charges of the attacks' type. Charges are "shared" between charge-up attacks so the first attack will apply a stage 1 effect and generate 1 charge, the second attack will apply a stage 2 effect and generate 1-2 charges, and the third attack will apply a stage 3 effect before the charges are reset and the cycle repeats.
    • Since charges are reset after the 3rd attack rather than before the first attack of the next cycle, it's impossible to have 3 charges of any single type; to get 3 charges, they must be of different types. A finishing move can be used at any point to consume the charges as usual.

Season 2:

  • Charge-up skills reworked
    • Instead of charges being generated one-at-a-time per charge-up attack and the effects only applying when consumed by a finishing move or normal attack:
    • Charge-up attacks immediately apply the attacks' effect of the appropriate stage (1-3) and generate charges until the character has that many charges of the attacks' type. Charges are "shared" between charge-up attacks so the first attack will apply a stage 1 effect and generate 1 charge, the second attack will apply a stage 2 effect and generate 1-2 charges, and the third attack will apply a stage 3 effect before the charges are reset and the cycle repeats.
    • Since charges are reset after the 3rd attack rather than before the first attack of the next cycle, it's impossible to have 3 charges of any single type; to get 3 charges, they must be of different types. A finishing move can be used at any point to consume the charges as usual.
  • synergy increased from 14% to 18%
  • damage decreased

Season 2:

  • Charge-up skills reworked
    • Instead of charges being generated one-at-a-time per charge-up attack and the effects only applying when consumed by a finishing move or normal attack:
    • Charge-up attacks immediately apply the attacks' effect of the appropriate stage (1-3) and generate charges until the character has that many charges of the attacks' type. Charges are "shared" between charge-up attacks so the first attack will apply a stage 1 effect and generate 1 charge, the second attack will apply a stage 2 effect and generate 1-2 charges, and the third attack will apply a stage 3 effect before the charges are reset and the cycle repeats.
    • Since charges are reset after the 3rd attack rather than before the first attack of the next cycle, it's impossible to have 3 charges of any single type; to get 3 charges, they must be of different types. A finishing move can be used at any point to consume the charges as usual.
  • synergy increased from 10% to 20%

Season 1:

  • attack rating bonus increased
  • synergy is now 10% (was 8%)

Shadow Warrior uses the two Skills you currently have active on Left and Right Click.

Number of Shadows can be increased by Whispering Mirage and Natalya's Odium.

Shadow Warriors equip randomly-generated equipment which can be viewed by using the Inspect hotkey (9) while hovering over a Shadow with the Unsummon skill on right-click. This equipment improves Damage, Attack Speed, Defense, and other Attributes. Chance to Cast effects from the equipment are functional.

Changelog

Season 13:

  • Traps set by master/warrior no longer “belong” to the player and instead are owned by the shadow
  • This mostly applies to blade sentinel and blade fury, which will now use the shadow’s weapon/stats for damage

Season 11:

  • Now displays quantity (to account for cases where you can summon more than one shadow).
  • AI rewritten and improved to use abilities more often instead of using normal attack.
  • Now snapshots the players skill synergies on summon instead of requiring the shadow to cast them in order to gain the benefits of the synergies (this behaviour now matches the current behaviour of Shadow Masters).
  • Now benefits from Weapon Block.
  • No longer has innate 50% block chance.

Season 10:

  • Fixed a bug that was causing stats to not properly apply

Season 7:

  • Item quality per level increased from 2 to 3
  • Shadow warrior base item quality increased from 18 to 20
  • Reworked Shadow Warrior equipment generation so that they will generate boots to increase their kick damage
  • Allowed inspecting shadow warriors gear (use unsummon skill to highlight the warrior and press inspect hotkey)

Season 6:

  • Shadow warrior AI has been updated
  • Shadow warrior cooldown reduced from 6 seconds to 2 second
  • Shadow warrior is now properly gaining its poison resist bonus

Season 5:

  • Shadow warrior base health in normal increased from 376 to 600
  • Shadow warrior base health in nightmare increased from 376 to 800
  • Shadow warrior base health in hell increased from 376 to 1000
  • Shadow warrior health per level reduced from 15% to 5%
  • Shadow warrior all resist scaling has been changed from +4 all resist per level capping at 75 to a diminishing return scaling from 5 to 90 (its all resist scaling now matches shadow master)

Shadow Master can use any Assassin Skill, even ones you don't have. Its AI is sophisticated and has no set Skill probabilities, but it tends to use more Martial Arts Skills than Traps, almost always keeps Venom and Blade Shield active, and alternates between Fade and Burst of Speed.

To prevent "double dipping" of damage bonuses, Poison Damage added to your attacks is calculated using only the base skill damage and the skill synergy bonus at the time of casting. Mastery damage (from any Poison Skill Damage +% on equipment) is applied on every attack.

Venom's 1-second Poison Length overrides Poison Length values from item-based sources of Poison Damage, but not Skill-based sources. For more information on calculating Poison Damage/Length, see here.

Listed Poison Damage is the rounded total over the 1 second duration. For calculating total character Poison Damage, the below "per frame" unrounded numbers may be useful:

Blade Sentinel is classified as a summoned creature. It travels back and forth between the point it was cast from and the target location. It travels 24 Yards per second and deals damage for 2 seconds, although startup and death animations make it appear to last longer. Its collision radius is 2 Yards.

When Blade Sentinel changes direction, it explodes, doing 75% weapon damage in the explosion radius as long as it has been 0.48 Seconds (12 frames) since the last explosion. There is no animation for this explosion. Blade Sentinel's explosion benefits fully from all forms of Resistance Pierce -% at full effect, but does not deal Blade Sentinel's skill damage or receive the flat Attack Rating (it will receive the Attack Rating +%).

Blade Sentinel Receives Bonuses From:

  • 50% of your Physical Resistance Pierce
  • Blade Fury: +12% Damage per Level
  • Blade Shield: +12% Damage per Level

Blade Fury uses your Main Hand weapon to perform a ranged attack. If dual wielding, normal rules regarding attack speed and affixes apply. Blades are normal projectiles, requiring Pierce Chance to pierce enemies.

Blades last 1.12 seconds (28 frames). Each Blade splits into 3 Blades when it hits a wall or other terrain (100% chance to split), or an enemy (50% chance), 3 splits maximum. Every time a blade splits it loses 0.08 seconds (2 frames) from its remaining duration.

Life and Mana Leech work at 75% effectiveness on all Blades; Chance to Cast effects are reduced by 80% on split Blades.

Blade Fury Receives Bonuses From:

  • Blade Sentinel: +10% Damage per Level
  • Blade Shield: +10% Damage per Level

Blade Shield in Project Diablo 2 is a Strike, but not an Attack. This means Blade Shield does not use weapon durability, and "on Striking" but not "on Attack" Chance to Cast effects will function. Blade Shield will also apply Crushing Blow, Open Wounds, and Life & Mana after each Kill, but not many other effects normally applied by weapons. If dual wielding, Blade Shield only uses your Main Hand weapon.

Blade Shield checks Attack Rating/Defense when Striking an enemy, but Blade Shield from Innocence does not (it will always hit).

Blade Shield Receives Bonuses From:

  • Blade Sentinel: +10% Damage per Level
  • Blade Fury: +10% Damage per Level

Other Sources: Innocence (level 8-12)

Outgoing projectiles do full damage but cannot hit a target multiple times (commonly called "shotgunning"). Returning projectiles do 30% damage but can hit a target multiple times.

Split Throw Receives Bonuses From:

  • Concentrate: +12% Damage per Level
  • Increased Speed: +12% Damage per level
Changelog

Season 13:

  • Added a new ability “Split Throw”
  • Throws your main hand throwing weapon splitting it into multiple projectiles which return to you after reaching their max distance (returning projectiles will always pierce)
  • Returning projectiles can shotgun (Initial outgoing projectiles cannot)
  • Gains an additional projectile every 5 levels (capping at 7 projectiles)

Changelog

Season 12:

  • Base enhanced damage bonus increased from +30% to +40%
  • Enhanced damage per level increased from 4% to 6%

Season 10:

  • Fixed a bug that was causing Whirlwind's range to cap at a range adder of 2
  • Changed Whirlwind to prioritize targeting the closest enemy

Season 5:

  • Whirlwind no longer attempts to do a normal attack when out of mana
  • Whirlwind no longer attacks in place during a namelock and will now whirlwind back and forth through the monster
  • Whirlwind damage per level reduced from 5% to 4%
  • Whirlwind base enhanced damage bonus reduced from 35% to 30%
  • Whirlwind now attacks 20% slower when dual wielding (6 frames during dual wielding compared to 5 when using a two handed weapon)

Season 4:

  • When dual wielding Whirlwind now swings with both weapons each attack
  • Whirlwind enhanced damage per level increased from 4% per level to 5%
  • Whirlwind starting damage and attack bonuses increased by 10%

Season 3:

  • prerequisites changed (now requires Double Swing instead of Frenzy)
  • Whirlwinds base attack rating reduced from 240% to 80%
  • Whirlwinds attack rating per level increased from 5% to 6%

Season 2:

  • has been reworked to have melee splash and to use proc effects, but now attacks at 5 frames fixed instead of 4 and now attacks one target per attack instead of two (it is now much stronger for AoE clearing)
    • For clarity: Whirlwind works the same as it did in LoD, but the speed of which it will determine its hit checks is now once every 5 frames across the board (rendering IAS useless for Whirlwind). For dual-wielding Whirlwind, the first 5 frame check will attack with the primary weapon, and every 5 frames afterward the weapon used to attack will alternate, as a result of the "one target per attack" change. This indicates that dual-wielding Whirlwind will have large redundancy, as you can only ever attack with one weapon at a time.
  • Enhanced Damage bonus at Level 1 reduced from +50% to +25%
  • Enhanced Damage bonus per level has reduced from +6% to +4%

Season 1:

  • moved in the skill tree
  • prerequisites reduced from 5 to 3 (no longer requires Bash, Stun, Leap, Leap Attack, now requires Frenzy, Berserk)
  • Movement speed increased by character's FRW speed
  • Now also scales velocity at 4% per level
  • bonus attack rating now starts at 240% (was 0%)
  • damage bonus increased to 50% + 6% per level (was -50% + 8%)
  • Will not apply splash damage from melee weapons

Fissure opens a damage vent at a random location within its radius every (Vent Frequency) for its listed duration. Each vent has a next hit delay of 0.2 seconds (5 frames).

The listed duration of 2.2 seconds (55 frames) only describes the "Vent making" portion of the skill. Each damage vent lasts 3.36 seconds (84 frames).

Volcano spawns debris every 0.08 seconds (2 frames) for the first 5 seconds of its duration. Debris travels for 0.64 seconds (16 frames) to a random location within the distance radius, and damages on impact (0.16 second/4 frame next hit delay). Volcano also does its damage if an enemy contacts the Volcano cone itself (0.24 second/6 frame next hit delay).

Tornado deals damage in two ways: on collision, and periodically (every 0.6 seconds/15 frames) inside its damage radius. These are considered different sources of damage and do not trigger each other's next hit delay.

Tornado lasts 3 seconds, traveling a maximum of 16 Yards. However its path randomly "meanders", not always traveling exactly to where Tornado was targeted.

Tornado reduces the current Cooldown of Gust by 0.52 seconds (13 frames) when cast.

Poison Creepers do not Attack; they emerge from the ground under their target, creating a vine patch that spreads outward.

Each vine patch "growth" spawns two more vine patches in a random outward direction from the center patch 0.36 seconds (9 frames) after the previous patch.
Vine patches have a 2 yard radius, are functionally identical to poison clouds, and last 4 seconds.

Creepers cannot be targeted or attacked, but can be damaged and killed (by projectiles and AoE damage) while above ground.

Poison Creeper can break Poison Immunity. See Reducing Resistances for more information.

Poison Creeper benefits from neither Poison Resistance Pierce -% (like most summoned creatures), nor +% Poison Skill Damage/Mastery (unlike most other summoned creatures).

Number of Revives can be increased further with Blood Raven's Charge, Sacred Totem, and the Eternity Runeword.

Revives retain most of their Attributes, Skills and AI behavior they had as enemies, and thus have an extremely wide variety of potential stats, skills, & damage.

Poison and Curse Duration Reduction has a cap of -75%, however Poison (but not Curse) Duration has a +100% penalty in Hell Difficulty making its effective cap -175%.

Cleansing Aura's active Curse/Poison Duration Reduction works independently from matching stats on equipment (and Cleansing's own Passive bonus):

Instead of reducing the total Duration when the Curse/Poison is inflicted, Cleansing "pulses" its effect every 2 seconds, reducing a Curse/Poison's remaining Duration by the Aura's percentage.

Other Sources: Act 3 Mercenary, Plague (level 15-17)

Changelog

Season 12 Patch #3:

  • Now player conviction overrides monster conviction at the same level, otherwise higher level takes priority like normal (practically this means a player/mercenary wearing an Infinity will only be affected by Aura enchanted enemies with Conviction in Zones with Area level 88 or higher)

Season 10:

  • Reduced the level 1 radius of Conviction by 18%

Season 1:

  • radius is increased and now scales with levels
  • enemy defense now starts at -19% (was -49%) and scales slightly more with levels but caps at -75% (was -100%)
  • enemy resistance reductions are 2/5 of their previous values - immunities are lowered at 1/2 effectiveness (was 1/5), so Conviction breaks the same immunities (and can break more immunities above level 25)

For a detailed explanation of Vengeance's mechanics, see below.

Vengeance Mechanics
Vengeance Damage
  • Vengeance deals Fire, Lightning, and Cold Damage. This damage is calculated from 3 sources in order:
  1. Weapon Damage
    • Vengeance converts 100% of most Weapon Damage into Elemental damage.
      • Included Damage: Physical weapon damage, Fire/Lightning/Cold damage from items (equipment and charms).
      • Excluded Damage: Poison damage, Magic damage (unconfirmed), Fire/Cold/Lightning Attack damage granted by spells (Paladin Auras and Cold/Fire Enchant).
        • Critical Damage, Crushing Blow, Life Leech, etc. are also excluded from Vengeance itself but since Vengeance is a weapon Attack, these attributes (and the above ones) will have a (small) effect on the normal weapon hit and melee splash.
    • This conversion is 1:1 for all 3 Elements, not split into 3 Elements.
      • For example, 100 weapon damage will turn into 100 Fire, 100 Cold, and 100 Lightning Damage, not 33 damage of each.
  2. Skill Damage
    • Vengeance's flat Elemental Skill Damage is then added to the Converted Damage for each Element.
    • The total Damage is then multiplied by the Skill Elemental Damage +%. The Synergy bonuses are added to the % here, and all Synergies apply to all three Damage types.
      • For example, the Holy Fire synergy adds up to 40% Damage to all three elements, not just Fire Damage.
  3. Mastery Damage
    • +% Elemental Skill Damage/Mastery then applies.
    • Each type of Mastery applies to each element individually.
      • For example, Level 6 Resist Fire Aura (or two 5% Fire Facets) will increase the Fire Damage of Vengeance by 10%, but not its Cold or Lightning Damage.
Vengeance Chaining
  • Vengeance does its damage in its radius, and any enemy hit by Vengeance has a chance to chain Vengeance, instantly repeating its effect and radius around that enemy.
  • Vengeance has no Next Hit Delay, meaning an enemy in range of multiple Vengeance radii can be hit by Vengeance multiple times.
  • This chaining will repeat until there are no more enemies to hit, or it reaches the maximum chain distance.

Vengeance Receives Bonuses From:

  • Holy Fire: +2% Elemental Damage per Level
  • Holy Freeze: +2% Elemental Damage per Level
  • Holy Shock: +2% Elemental Damage per Level
  • Conviction: +2% Elemental Damage per Level

Other Sources: Kingslayer

Frozen Orb's primary Orb lasts 1.8 seconds (45 frames) and travels 14 Yards. While traveling, it fires an Ice Bolt outward in a "spray" pattern every 0.04 seconds (every frame). Each Ice Bolt also has a range of 14 yards. The primary Orb does not deal damage, only the Ice Bolts do. When the Orb hits a wall or other impassable terrain, or at the end of its duration, the Orb explodes releasing 16 Ice Bolts in all directions. The explosion's Ice Bolts will not do damage if the Orb hit terrain, but they will if the Orb reached the end of its duration.

Frozen Orb has no Cooldown in Project Diablo 2, but it was changed to the "Slow Spell" Cast Rate.

Static Field can break Lightning Immunity. See Reducing Resistances for more information.

Static Field's 25% Life reduction is Lightning Damage, reduced (or increased) normally by enemy Lightning Resistance.

Because the current Life check is before the damage calculation, Static Field's total damage can exceed the 55/70/85% cap. (see example below)

Static Field Damage Example

Level 33 Static Field (-32%) is cast against an Enemy with 50% Lightning Resistance in Hell difficulty

Cast 1: 12.5% Damage (25% * 50% Resistance)

Enemy reduced to 87.5% HP and 18% Lightning Resistance

Cast 2: 17.9375% Damage ((25% of 87.5% or 21.875%) * 18% Resistance)

Enemy reduced to 69.5625% Life and still at 18% Lightning Resistance

Cast 3: Enemy is below 85% Life, damage portion of Static Field does not effect enemy (Resistance debuff still refreshed)

Static Field receives bonuses from:

  • Lightning Mastery: +0.2 Seconds Duration per Level

When Struck Sources: Aetherwing (35% cast level 40), Epiphany (25% cast level 27), Cow King's Leathers Set Bonuses (25% Chance cast Level 18), Hwanin's Refuge (20% cast level 9)

On Striking Sources: Stormspire (75% cast level 40), Stormlash & Schaefer's Hammer (20% cast level 25), Hwanin's Justice (20% cast level 16), Crescent Moon (Weapon) (24/12% cast level 13)

On Casting Sources: Spire of Lazarus (30% cast level 15)

Energy Shield does not apply to poison damage.

For a detailed explanation of how Energy Shield absorbs and multiplies damage, see below.

Energy Shield Mechanics & Examples
  • Energy Shield's Damage Absorption % (soft levels) is applied first, and determines how much of the incoming damage is "sent" to Life and Mana, respectively.
    • Damage still "sent" to Life then gets normal damage reductions (PDR/MDR/Resistances/Absorb/etc) applied.
  • Damage "sent" to Mana then has the Mana Loss Multiplier % (hard levels) applied.
  • The resulting number then drains or "damages" your Mana pool.
  • If the full amount of incoming damage would reduce Mana below 0, Energy Shield will only absorb damage equal to the amount that will drain the rest of your remaining Mana, and the excess will damage your Life unaffected by Energy Shield.
    • Energy shield stays active when out of mana in PD2.

Example 1: Level 40 Energy Shield (20 Hard Levels)

  • 100 Damage Taken
  • Energy Shield Absorbs 90% of that - 90 damage "sent" to Mana, 10 damage "sent" to Life
  • Mana Loss Multiplier applies to the 90 damage "sent" to Mana (87.5% at Hard Level 20)
    • 90 * 87.5% = 78.75
  • Mana is reduced/"damaged" by 78.75, Life is damaged by 10.
    • Other damage reductions will still apply to the Life damage.

Example 2: Level 6 Energy Shield (6 Hard Levels)

  • 100 Damage Taken
  • Energy Shield Absorbs 25% of that - 25 damage "sent" to Mana, 75 damage "sent" to Life
  • Mana Loss Multiplier applies to the 25 damage "sent" to Mana (175% at Hard Level 6)
    • 25 * 175% = 43.75
  • Mana is reduced/"damaged" by 43.75, Life is damaged by 75.
    • Other damage reductions will still apply to the Life damage.

Example 3: Level 40 Energy Shield (20 Hard Levels) but only 50 mana remaining

  • 100 Damage Taken
  • Energy Shield Absorbs 90% of that - 90 damage "sent" to Mana, 10 damage "sent" to Life
  • Mana Loss Multiplier applies to the 90 damage "sent" to Mana (87.5% at Hard Level 20)
    • 90 * 87.5% = 78.75 damage
  • 78.75 is more than current mana (50), so Energy Shield will only absorb (50 / 87.5%) = 57.143 damage.
  • Mana is reduced/"damaged" by 50, Life is damaged by 42.857.
    • Other damage reductions will still apply to the Life damage.

While Energy Shield is calculated before any damage reductions as described above, Mana gained from "Damage Taken Gained as Mana when Hit" applies only to Life lost after all reductions. See the Amazon Basin Wiki on Energy Shield and Damage Taken Goes to Mana for details.

Other Sources: Uldyssian's Awakening (Level 30), Tempest & Epiphany (Level 16)

Blade Dance is a modified version of Whirlwind. It hits once every 0.2 seconds (5 frames) when using a single weapon or twice every 0.2 seconds when dual-wielding.

Blade Dance is categorized as an Assassin Martial Arts skill; in addition to "+X to All Skills", it also benefits from "+X to Assassin Skills" and "+X to Martial Arts (Assassin Only)" affixes.

Changelog

Season 12:

  • Now deals damage every 5th frame instead of every 4th.
  • Base enhanced damage reduced from 40% to 30%.
  • Enhanced damage per level reduced from 5% to 4%.

Season 10:

  • Base Enhanced Damage from +80% to +40%.
  • Base Enhanced Damage per level reduced from +8% to +5%.
    • Note: We wanted to maintain the power of Blade Dance Assassins but transition that power away from raw physical damage and more into the poison thematic.

Season 9:

  • Base damage reduced from 110% to 80%.
  • Enhanced damage per level reduced from 10% to 8%.

Season 7:

  • Base damage increased from 60% to 110%.
  • Base attack rating increased from 90% to 200%.
  • Attack rating per level increased from 6% to 15%.

Season 6:

  • Base enhanced damage bonus increased from 30% to 60%.
  • Enhanced damage per level increased from 4% to 10%.
  • Now counts as a Martial Arts skill and benefits from + to Martial Arts skills, + All Skills and + to Assassin skills.

Season 5:

  • Skill added (same as Whirlwind except it hits 1 frame faster).
  • Base velocity bonus increased from 0% to 20% (patch 6).
  • No longer locks the player in animation on level up (patch 6).
